verdict.rationale: Databricks documents its own versioning for automation-adjacent assets: notebooks have automatic versioning, SQL queries keep version history, agents deployed on Databricks Apps support git-based versioning, and the MLflow prompt registry offers Git-like versions with commit messages and rollback. None of this is documented as a versioned, reviewable, roll-back-able lifecycle for jobs or pipelines themselves, so the story is only partly delivered. Missing for 10: documented versioning and rollback for jobs/pipelines (automations proper), a review or approval workflow for automation changes, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Databricks notebooks provide real-time coauthoring in multiple languages, automatic versioning, and built-in data visualizations for developing code and presenting results.
Write and run SQL queries with integrated AI assistance, code comments, and version history.
Version and track prompts with Git-like versioning, commit messages, and rollback capabilities
This approach is ideal when you need custom server behavior, git-based versioning, or local IDE development.
